phrases.nuance_en: used when the time is short but the content is solid

dis.h: few in number or small in amount

p.n: 근소하다 means a very slight margin, so it cannot describe how many students are present.

Everything about life in Korea feels new.
Korean food is all new to me.

usage: 가격 = price (formal, on tags). 값 is the everyday word.

examples.en: The price of this bag is high.
The price is too high.

examples.en: I check the price of the clothes.

p.n: Same meaning; 값 is plainer and more everyday.

I have a lot of classes on Mondays.

explain_en: Teaching time itself (수업을 듣다), school or academy. Students say 수업을 들어요 (“listen to a class”), teachers say 수업을 해요 (“do a class”). Same class, different verbs.

examples.en: I practice pronunciation.
The pronunciation is hard.
Ben, your pronunciation is really good.
I practice my Korean pronunciation every morning.
How's my pronunciation? — It's very good.
This word has a strange pronunciation.

explain: 발음이 별로일 때는 “발음이 안 좋아요”라고 해요. “발음이 나빠요”는 너무 센 말이에요.

explain_en: If pronunciation isn't great, say 발음이 안 좋아요. 발음이 나빠요 sounds too harsh.

en: to be old; to be long-established

examples.en: It is an old house.
This building is very old.
This computer is old. It's too slow.

explain: '오래되다'는 건물, 카페, 책, 휴대폰처럼 사물이 생긴 지 오래됐을 때 써요(오래된 건물, 오래된 책). 사람의 나이에는 쓰지 않아요. 사람은 '나이가 많다'나 '늙다'를 써요.

phrases.nuance_en: Before a noun it becomes 오래된.
Use it to say something is not old.

phrases.en: The house is old, so it's a bit cold.
phrases.nuance_en: Connect with -아/어서 to give a reason.

dict_examples.ko: 쓰던 가전제품이 오래되고 낡아서 새것으로 바꿨다.
dict_examples.en: The appliance I'd been using was old and worn, so I replaced it with a new one.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: '오래되다' is for things that have been around a long time: a building, a café, a book, a phone (오래된 건물 an old building, 오래된 책 an old book). Don't use it for a person's age. For people, say 나이가 많다 or 늙다.
